_comment: Single source of truth for what every symbol is. A device's id (and detector training class) is '<symbol_family>.<symbol_variant>', e.g. 'switch.three_way'.
aliases.neca_v7: NECA 100-2013 glyph names (device_type/subtype) drawn as this device; aliases.devices_json: device_type strings of extracted *_DEVICES.json files.
family_aliases: extracted device types that only name a family (the variant is picked in review).
not_devices: names that never identify a device (older coarse detector classes, pre-catalog families); boxes carrying them are ignored by training.
non_electrical_types: extracted device types that are not electrical devices; never proposed.
legacy_detector_classes: class names of older coarse detectors -> family their proposals start as.
keyword_fallback: for unknown extracted device_type strings, first rule whose word occurs wins.

aliases.legend: how legend sheets describe the device. Each phrase lists words that must all occur in the description ('a|b' = either; '-word' = must not occur). The match covering the most description words wins; a tie between devices matches none. Words are compared after legend_synonyms rewrite the lowercased text (non-alphanumerics become spaces).
non_electrical_types also lists marks that are not devices at all (homerun_arrow: a circuit home-run annotation).

Every box anywhere (annotator, agents, model, DEVICES/SAM/CircuitNet/VLM proposals, training) is one of these devices, or '<family>.unspecified' while its exact device is not picked yet (label_schema.canonical_device).
renamed: former class ids -> the class they were merged into (no separate wall/ceiling-mounted versions; overlapping names folded). Old labels keep their meaning.
subtype_aliases: per family, subtypes that name a device by default (a plain receptacle is a duplex; plain GFCI = GFCI duplex; weatherproof = weatherproof duplex).
weatherproof_suffix: weatherproof is added on top of a receptacle device (duplex -> duplex_weatherproof, duplex_gfci -> duplex_gfci_weatherproof) when a source marks the device weatherproof.

augmentation._comment: Training-time geometry per device class (scripts_export_yolo_tiles.train_variant). A training tile is turned as a whole, symbol and nearby text together, by a multiple of 90 degrees counter-clockwise; a tile uses only the rotations every labelled device in it allows. Mirroring is never used: drawings never show mirrored letters or arrows (S3, GFI, WP, exit arrows). Symbols rotate with their walls, so 90/270 are realistic for all devices; letters in or beside a symbol are drafted to read from the bottom or the right and appear read-from-the-left in rotated blocks, but rarely upside down, so 180 is only for purely graphic symbols. Keys are a device (family.variant) or a family; a device key wins.
